images.title: Quarter of a turn
images.purpose: A straight angle is half a turn, so a right angle is a quarter of a full turn.
images.composition: Three circle diagrams in a row, each a simple circle outline, wide gaps between them.
images.exact_structure: Left: a circle with nothing shaded. Middle: a circle with exactly its left half shaded teal #0072B2 (half turn, a straight angle). Right: a circle with exactly one quarter shaded amber #E69F00 with a small square corner mark. All 3 circles exactly the same size, centre dots, outlines in grey #6B7280. Exactly 3 circles.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any of the following: circles of different sizes
images.takeaway: A right angle is 1/4 of a full turn.
images.description: Three equal circles: a full turn, a half turn shaded teal, and a quarter turn shaded amber with a right angle mark.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at each shaded part and say what fraction of the circle it is.

image_decisions.why: Seeing full, half and quarter turns on equal circles is one clear picture of the idea.
